SMTO-HTTP-0005 — Some sign-in details aren't in a form SMTO can use

GUID: 9c503bb7-8fe0-47c5-aa1e-285eb7249ac1
Slug: http-auth-values-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • A sign-in detail for this HTTP Connection was rejected before anything was sent, for example a username containing a colon (:), or a sign-in field the connection doesn't have.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select this HTTP Connection, and look at Username under Authentication settings. If Authentication is set to Basic, the username can't contain a colon (:). Basic sign-in uses the colon to separate the username from the password.
  2. If your username really contains a colon, ask the service's administrator for another username, or choose another sign-in method under Authentication that the service supports, such as Digest. SMTO blocks colons only for Basic sign-in, where the colon separates the username from the password.
  3. If SMTO itself supplied the sign-in details during a Task, tell it in the conversation to use only the sign-in fields this connection lists. SMTO rejects field names the connection doesn't define instead of guessing where they belong.
  4. Save, then select Test connection. The test confirms the corrected details are accepted.

What success looks like

  • Test connection reports Reachable and Authenticated, without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this HTTP Connection. Don't keep resubmitting the same details; they will be rejected the same way until the named field is fixed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HTTP credential validation failed: a Basic authentication username contains ':', or auth_values was not an object of at most 32 advertised value paths with scalar values.

What this means

  • A Basic username contains a colon, or auth_values is not a bounded object of at most 32 advertised scalar value paths. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A Basic username contains a colon, or auth_values is not a bounded object of at most 32 advertised scalar value paths.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare field names and value types with advertised authentication paths; check Basic username syntax privately.

How to fix it

  • For Basic auth, use a username without ':' or switch to another supported auth type such as Digest. For auth_values, supply only the value paths the connection advertises (username, password, token, value, OAuth fields or its declared login fields), each as a scalar, with at most 32 entries.
  • Correct the named credential fields and types through the supported authentication flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected values pass provider/profile validation without changing unrelated fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
